title: About RunLock and Texsolv
desc: RunLock has been made in Sweden by Texsolv since 1983: the loop idea from the Texsolv weaving heddle, braided from polyester in Tösse, Dalsland, and tested at SP. The story, the factory and the people.
heads: Born and raised in the cold north. The idea came from a loom. Tested, not just promised Who uses it Made to order Texsolv AB Elsewhere
text: > About RunLock Born and raised in the cold north. RunLock has been developed and made in Sweden by Texsolv since 1983, today at Vitlanda in Tösse, in the forests of Dalsland. One factory braids every metre, tests it, cuts it and ships it. About Texsolv AB Contact The idea came from a loom. Texsolv was founded in 1977 by Sune Ivarsson in Alafors, north of Gothenburg, to make heddles, cord and tie-up sets for hand weaving looms. The heddles are made of a polyester cord with a loop at each end, and the cord has loops along its length so that it can be fastened anywhere without a knot. Weavers all over the world use it, and many of the leading loom makers fit it as standard. The founder also needed a flexible, reliable rope outdoors: for pulling game out of the forest, tying down loads and hanging tools in the workshop. He took the loop design from the heddle cord, gave it a stronger braid and built-in stretch, and in 1983 RunLock was born. The name says what it does: the rope runs through its own loops and locks. Today the company is run by Thomas Ivarsson, Sune's son, and both Texsolv and RunLock are made at Vitlanda in Tösse, south of Åmål on the west shore of Lake Vänern. The ropes are braided on the company's own machines, under its own quality control, from 100 % polyester. Tested, not just promised In 2016 one rope of each size was pulled to breaking at SP, the Swedish national testing institute (now RISE). The published breaking strengths are set with a margin below the measured results, and the stretch figures on this site are the elongations from that test. The test, size by size → Who uses it Hunters, dog owners, boat owners, farmers and anyone with a trailer, a roof rack or a washing line. RunLock has also been supplied to armed forces, police and rescue services, and to professionals in forestry and transport, who all put value on the same three things: flexibility, quality and simplicity. Made to order Because the rope is braided here, it can be made differently for a larger order: another size, loops only where they are needed, another colour, cut to length. title: Questions and answers
desc: Answers about RunLock: how the knot-free lock works, which size to choose, how strong the rope is, towing, cutting, washing, joining two ropes, the leashes, colours and where to buy.
heads: Questions and answers.
text: > FAQ Questions and answers. The questions we get about the rope, the sizes, the locks and the leashes, answered short. Something missing? Ask us → What is RunLock? RunLock is a braided polyester rope with a loop every few centimetres. Two strands run side by side and are braided together at intervals; the free stretch between two joins is a loop. Because the rope can be pushed through its own loops, you can make a grip, a snare, a fixed loop or a lock in a second, without a knot, and undo it just as fast. It has been made in Sweden by Texsolv since 1983. How does it lock without a knot? Every lock is the same move: the rope, or a fold of it, goes through one of its own loops. Under load the loop closes on the part that runs through it, and the harder you pull, the harder it grips. Slack it off and the grip opens again, because nothing has been tied. The four locks, step by step → Which size should I choose? No 4 (4 mm) for washing lines, tent lines and hanging gear; No 6 for leashes and light lines; No 8 (6 mm) is the all-round size for cargo, trailers and roof racks; No 12 for heavier tie-downs; No 16 (10 mm) for dragging game and pulling by hand; No 20 (12 mm) for towing. When in doubt, take the next size up. All sizes with figures → How strong is it? The published breaking strengths run from 170 kg for No 4 to 700 kg for No 20. They are set with a margin below the forces measured when one rope of each size was pulled to breaking at SP, the Swedish national testing institute (now RISE), in 2016; the No 20 held 843 kg in that test. The rating is the strength of the rope, not the load to work it at every day: pick a size with strength to spare. The test, size by size → Can I tow a car with it? Yes, with the No 20, the towing line. Make a running loop over the tow ball, or a quick loop with fixed release through a closed ring, and start the pull gently: the 25 % stretch in the rope smooths the first metre out. For a heavy vehicle, use two lines together. RunLock is not a certified lifting sling and should not be used for lifting loads over people or for climbing. Does it really not lose strength at the lock? A knot bends a rope sharply around itself and the outer fibres carry far more than the inner ones. A RunLock lock loads the braided join instead, which is made to carry the load straight through, so the rope keeps its full strength in the first loop and in every situation after it. In the SP test the ropes broke at the end loops around the shackles, not in the braid. Can I cut it to length? Yes. Cut in the middle of a loop, across both strands, then melt each cut end briefly with a lighter and press the two strands together so the end is sealed in one piece. A cut length is a complete tool: there is no eye to splice and no hardware to fit. That is also how the bulk roll is used. Can I wash it? Machine wash at 40 °C without fabric softener and let it dry hanging. Mud, salt and resin come out, and the colours stay. Polyester takes up almost no water, so the rope does not swell, stiffen or get heavy when wet. Does it float, and does it stand sun, salt and oil? It does not float: polyester is heavier than water. It has good resistance to UV light, salt water and petroleum products, keeps its flexibility in the cold, and a frozen RunLock still releases with one pull. Keep it away from exhausts and open fire: polyester melts at about 250 °C. Can I join two ropes? Yes. Pass the end of one rope through a loop of the other, then back through its own loop. The join holds like the rope itself and comes apart with one pull when the load is off. Join two ropes to reach further or to pull with more force. What is the difference between the dog leash and the hunting leash? Both are one piece of RunLock with a neck loop that is a running loop with a stop, so it tightens only as far as you set it: the controlled semi-choke. The dog leash is 1.8 m for the daily walk. The hunting leash is 1.8 to 2.7 m and its handle opens into a loop that fits around the upper body, for hands-free work in the forest. The leashes → What colours are there? Fluorescent orange, fluorescent yellow, blue, black and white. The leashes and the snowmobile set come in a two-colour braid, black with fluorescent yellow or orange. Other colours are possible for larger orders. Colours → Where can I buy it? In the webshop , shipped worldwide from Sweden. Shops and wholesalers open a business account in the same webshop and buy at reseller terms. Wholesale → Can you make other sizes, lengths or colours? Yes, for larger orders. The rope is braided on our own machines in Tösse, so size, loop spacing, length and colour are all open: thinner than No 4 or thicker than No 20, loops only at the ends, a private colour. Made to your spec → Is it safe for lifting people or climbing? No. RunLock is a rope for pulling, tying down, hanging and leading. It is not a certified lifting sling or a climbing rope, and it must not be used for lifting loads over people or for any use where a failure would put someone at risk. text: > Home › The rope The rope A rope made of loops. RunLock is a braided polyester rope whose two halves are braided together at regular intervals and run free in between. Every free stretch is a loop. That is the whole idea, and everything the rope can do follows from it. How it is made → Specifications How it is made Two sides. Joined every few centimetres. The rope is braided from polyester threads in two groups, one for each side. The size number is the number of threads in each group: a No 4 has 4 + 4 threads, a No 20 has 20 + 20. Every thread is three yarns twisted together. On the braiding machine the two groups are braided through each other for a short stretch, then run apart, then braided together again. Each time they meet, the groups swap sides. The free stretch is the loop. The braided stretch is the join that carries the load. 8–40 Threads The size number is the thread count per side: No 4 is 4 + 4 threads, No 20 is 20 + 20. Each thread is three twisted yarns. 40–65 mm Loop length Shorter loops on the thin sizes, longer on the thick. The loop is where the rope goes through itself. 100 % Strength in every loop There is no knot to weaken the rope. The braided join carries the full breaking strength, from the first loop to the last. Why a loop holds No knot. Just the rope through itself. Every RunLock lock is the same move: the rope, or a fold of it, is pushed through one of its own loops. When the rope is loaded, the loop is pulled tight around the part that passes through it. The harder you pull, the harder it grips. Slack it off and the grip opens again, because nothing has been tied. That is why the rope does not lose strength at the lock. A knot bends a rope sharply around itself, and the fibres on the outside of the bend carry far more than the fibres on the inside. RunLock loads the braided join, which is made to carry the load straight through. The four locks differ only in how the rope is led through the loop: sliding (the running loop), fixed (the fixed loop), locked but quick to release (the quick loop) or wrapped around an anchor (the securing lock). Because the loops sit every few centimetres, every lock is adjustable in steps of one loop. Move the end one loop forward and the rope is one loop shorter. There is nothing to retie. Try it yourself, on screen → Joining two ropes Two RunLocks join loop to loop: pass the end of one through a loop of the other, then back through its own loop. The join holds like the rope itself and comes apart with one pull when the load is off. Join two No 16 to pull with more force, or a No 8 to a No 4 to reach a little further. Every size has been pull-tested at SP, the Swedish national testing institute: a new rope, loaded in a straight pull until it breaks. The No 20 held 843 kg before it broke. We rate it at 700 kg, and every size gets its rating the same way, well below the force it actually held. The rating is the strength of the rope, not the load to work it at every day. Tying down and pulling means jerks, wet rope and corners, so pick a size with strength to spare. For towing, that is the No 20 and a gentle start: the stretch in the rope smooths the pull out. RunLock is a rope for pulling, tying down, hanging and leading. It is not a lifting sling or a climbing rope, and it is not certified for lifting loads over people. Stretch Every size stretches by a fifth to a quarter of its length before it breaks, 21 to 25 % in the SP test, and springs back when the load is off. In a towing line that stretch is what turns a jerk into a pull: the rope takes up the first metre of movement gently instead of passing the shock straight into the two cars. In a tie-down it is what keeps the load tight: the rope is slightly stretched when you lock it, and it keeps pulling as the load settles.
